about.title: Lawndale Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Lawndale sits in a busy stretch of Los Angeles County, wedged near the I-405 corridor and industrial pockets along Rosecrans Avenue and Inglewood Avenue, where warehouses, distribution centers, auto shops, and small manufacturers keep a lot of people working with their hands and on their feet. When someone gets hurt on the job here, the first stop is usually workers' compensation, which covers medical care and partial wage replacement no matter who caused the accident. But workers' comp isn't always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a road like Hawthorne Boulevard contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside the comp claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured workers in Lawndale with an independent attorney who can look at the full picture and explain what options actually apply to a specific situation, at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Lawndale Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Look Beyond the Comp Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but if a third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker played a role, a separate injury claim may be worth exploring alongside it.

items.title: We Know the Reporting Clock Matters
items.desc: California workers generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to their employer, and missing that window can complicate a claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: We Understand Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: An employer cannot legally punish, demote, or fire a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help address concerns if that happens.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near the I-405 in Lawndale. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: It might be both. Workers' comp typically applies since the injury happened on the job, but if another driver caused the crash, that driver's negligence could support a separate third-party injury claim. An independent attorney can review the details and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: My employer told me not to file a claim. Can they do that?
items.answer: No. Retaliation against a worker for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim is illegal in California. If you're facing pressure not to report, it's worth talking to an independent attorney about your options.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim after a workplace injury in Lawndale?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. Workers' comp reporting has its own much shorter 30-day window, so it helps to get guidance on both timelines as soon as possible.
